Bug_Title: Expressions used in "assert" should not produce side effects
Bug_Details:
Since assert statements aren’t executed by default (they must be enabled with JVM flags) developers should never rely on their
execution the evaluation of any logic required for correct program function.
Noncompliant code example
assert myList.remove(myList.get(0));  // Noncompliant
Compliant solution
boolean removed = myList.remove(myList.get(0));
assert removed;
Bug_Explanation: The assert statement in the main method uses the remove method to remove the first element in the list, which produces a side effect by modifying the list. This is not allowed in an assert statement.
Trigger_Explanation: The assert statement in the test method uses the remove method to remove the first element in the list, which produces a side effect by modifying the list. This is not allowed in an assert statement.
